title: Jobs in the Wild
hook: Emily learns the valet lot lost to a photo of level 3B taken at midnight.
counterintuition: The jobs lens is claimed to travel across any domain, but it only proves itself when you take it somewhere no case study has visited yet and let observable evidence decide.
tryThisNow: Pick a product outside your work. Write: the circumstance that triggers the hire, the progress you seek, and the alternatives you considered. If the job differs from the stated purpose, you have proved portability.
keyTakeaway: Carry the three-part diagnostic into a domain you have never mapped before. If the evidence still holds, you have proved portability rather than assumed it.

breakdown.fastRead: Emily interviews frequent flyers about valet parking and expects the answer to be about price or ease. What she hears is about certainty. A traveler who lands at midnight after a delay needs to know exactly which level the car is on before the doors open. A self-park space circled in a photo on a phone does that job. Valet cannot. The three-part method travels to an airport garage and finds something nobody predicted from the category label. That is portability proved, not assumed.
breakdown.deepRead:
A lens that only works on famous examples is a story, not a method. The discipline test comes when you carry it into a domain nobody has written up, apply the three questions plainly, and see whether the answer holds against what you can actually observe. That is the only version of portability that proves anything.

André runs a community garden and expects underused plots to signal commitment problems. Three rounds of interviews produce a different picture entirely. Some people hired the plot for stress relief through physical work. Others hired it for the neighbor in the adjacent row, a specific person whose presence made the whole activity worth driving across town for. When that neighbor moved away, the plot went fallow. The job evaporated. The dirt was still there. The garden was still there. The person had not failed to commit. The circumstance that made the hire meaningful had quietly ended, and no renewal letter was going to fix that.

Portability works because the structure of human progress is more stable than any individual product category. People keep seeking movement from a constrained current state toward a recognizable better state. The category changes. The pressure, the substitute, and the measure of success are what you have to re-earn with local evidence each time. Portability is proven when local evidence, not category logic, defines the substitute set. Import a conclusion without re-earning the evidence and you are borrowing confidence, not running the method.

The method travels. The conclusions do not.
breakdown.fullRead:
The three-part diagnostic has a simple form: name the circumstance that makes the hire active, describe the progress being sought, and identify the real substitute set. The questions do not change across domains. The answers must come from evidence gathered in the new setting, not from confidence built in the old one.

Chiara is designing software for freelance accountants and expects churn data to point at an invoicing workflow problem. She digs into which features retained users engage most. The CLIENT NOTES field, by a wide margin. Not the invoice templates. Not the payment tracking dashboard. The CLIENT NOTES field, used to log call tone, client mood, and relationship anxiety about a particular account. Retained users are not hiring a billing tool. They are hiring a relationship-anxiety management system that happens to also do billing. The job is legible only because she followed the evidence rather than her prediction.

This is what portability means in practice. You do not carry the answer. You carry the discipline of asking: what situation made this person reach for something, what would a better version of this situation feel like, and what else was this person comparing in that moment. Those questions can survive any domain shift. The answers cannot travel with you.

James evaluates whether to add pronunciation-scoring AI to a language exchange app. The feature addresses a real stated want. Then he looks at cancellation data sorted by what the partner said in the last message. Sessions where the partner wrote something like you are easy to understand have cancellation rates nearly thirty percent lower than sessions where the user scored ninety percent on the accuracy metric. The job the app is hired to do is lower the emotional cost of trying without feeling like a burden. Pronunciation AI answers the stated want and misses the hired job.

Ingrid predicts her color consultation service will lift premium paint sales. At 10:15 in the morning, she watches consultees return to the floor and pick the same mid-range color their neighbor used. Exit interviews repeat the same line: I just needed someone to say I was not going to ruin it. The job is permission to proceed, not color expertise. The consultation earned its value by removing the fear of a visible mistake in front of neighbors.

Kiran adds speed designations to pool lap lanes expecting the fastest swimmers to sort themselves in and improve flow. The fast lane fills instead because the designation signals serious swimmers only, not fastest. Swimmers who are fast but do not identify as serious avoid it even when it is empty. The job served by the designation is social belonging in a peer-defined group. Kiran misread his own fix and built a belonging barrier while solving a flow problem.

Each case holds one structure: someone carried the questions into an unmapped domain, stayed close to observable behavior, and found an answer the category label would never have suggested. The three-part diagnostic travels. The conclusions must be earned each time. That re-earning is not a limitation of the method. It is what the method is.

examples.title: Emily hears why a photo of level 3B beats the valet lot

planSpec.stakes: quality and price gap does not explain the hiring pattern
planSpec.requiredBeat: a frequent traveler reveals the job is certainty of retrieval under stress, not price; a circled photo is the real substitute

examples.scenario: At 10:30 a.m., "Last time you used valet?" Emily asks, recorder between them. The traveler shows a phone photo: concrete pillar marked 3B, her car hood in the corner. "I landed at midnight. Delay. Forty minutes before the last hotel shuttle. That is why I do not valet. I need to know exactly which level my car is on before the elevator opens. Valet cannot promise that after a delay." Emily's notepad says quality gap, price gap. She crosses both out.
examples.whatToDo: Run the three-part diagnostic on the retrieval moment, not the drop-off. Ask what circumstance makes the hire active, what certainty feels like when it works, and what substitute already does that job for the traveler.
examples.whyItMatters: Price and quality are not the competing variables here. The real substitute is a self-park space documented with a phone photo. Valet loses that contest by design, regardless of quality improvements.

examples.title: André finds job evaporation in the underused plots

planSpec.stakes: underuse looks like commitment failure but is job evaporation
planSpec.requiredBeat: interviews reveal three distinct jobs; plots hired for the social belonging job go underused when the neighboring plot-holder moves away

examples.scenario: Warm soil and a hose running in the next row. André, the community garden manager, kneels beside untended beds in late July, plot stakes still bearing April names. Three rounds of interviews reveal three distinct jobs: stress relief through physical work, fresh produce access, and belonging with the neighbor in the adjacent plot. The third group drove across town for one specific person. When that neighbor moved away in June, those plots went fallow within two weeks. Commitment had nothing to do with it.
examples.whatToDo: Segment the plot-holder pool by the job that drove the hire. Treat social-belonging jobs as weather-dependent: when the circumstance that made the hire active changes, plan for turnover, not renewal campaigns.
examples.whyItMatters: Job evaporation is not churn. The gardener did not fail to commit. The circumstance that made the garden worth hiring quietly ended, and no retention letter will reconstruct it.

examples.title: Chiara finds relationship anxiety inside the invoicing software

planSpec.stakes: churn data points away from invoicing and toward an unexpected job
planSpec.requiredBeat: retained users engage the CLIENT NOTES field most; the job is relationship-anxiety management, not billing speed

examples.scenario: Chiara, the product lead, sorts feature engagement by twelve-month retention correlation. The CLIENT NOTES field wins, not invoice templates or payment tracking. Retained users log call tone, client mood, and relationship anxiety. Exit interviews with lapsed users almost never mention billing; several mention not knowing where they stood with their biggest client. The postmortem conclusion: the product's best job is emotional bookkeeping for freelancers afraid a client relationship is quietly going wrong.
examples.whatToDo: Redesign the onboarding sequence to surface CLIENT NOTES early. Frame the product around relationship confidence over billing efficiency in positioning and feature priorities.
examples.whyItMatters: Retained users hired a relationship-anxiety management tool that also handles invoices. A billing-speed roadmap would have spent the next year improving the part of the product that was not driving retention.

examples.title: James weighs pronunciation AI against the cancellation data

planSpec.stakes: pronunciation AI answers the stated want and misses the hired job
planSpec.requiredBeat: sessions where partner says 'you're easy to understand' cancel less than high-accuracy sessions; job is lowering the emotional cost of trying; James faces the decision

examples.scenario: You are James. Top feature request: pronunciation-scoring AI, 340 upvotes. You pull cancellation data sorted by the last partner message before a session ends without rescheduling. Sessions where the partner wrote you are easy to understand cancel thirty percent less often than high-accuracy-score sessions. The accuracy score answers what users asked for. The partner's words answer the fear of being a burden. You must decide which one to build.
examples.whatToDo: Test a lightweight partner-feedback prompt before committing to the pronunciation AI build. Measure whether explicit reassurance from a human partner reduces cancellations more than any accuracy metric improvement.
examples.whyItMatters: The stated want and the hired job are not the same. Pronunciation AI solves what users asked for and misses the emotional cost that drives attrition. Building it without this distinction is a bet on the wrong variable.

examples.title: At 10:15am, Ingrid predicts premium paint, hears permission to proceed

planSpec.stakes: color consultation service expected to lift premium sales
planSpec.requiredBeat: prediction is premium paint sales; reality is mid-range plus the job of permission to proceed; exit line reveals the job

examples.scenario: At 10:15 a.m. Ingrid logs her prediction: premium paint sales will rise among consultees. By noon, five of six consultees return to the floor and pick the same mid-range brand their neighbor used. At the register one buyer says: "You told me it would look fine with our trim. I just needed someone to say I was not going to ruin it." Ingrid reads back through her notes. Every session ended with the same line. The consultation earned its fee by removing the fear of a visible mistake in front of neighbors. Ingrid must decide whether to rebuild the consultation pitch around this job rather than premium paint recommendations.
examples.whatToDo: Reframe the consultation service around the permission job. Train staff to name the anxiety, validate the choice early, and close with a plain statement that the decision is defensible. Track confidence ratings, not paint tier.
examples.whyItMatters: The consultation is not being hired for expertise. It is being hired for the relief that follows a clear, trusted answer from another person. Pricing and staffing built around color knowledge will underserve the actual job.

examples.title: Kiran misreads his own lane fix at the pool

planSpec.domain: public swimming pool lap lane scheduling
planSpec.stakes: speed designations created a belonging problem instead of solving a flow problem
planSpec.requiredBeat: fast lane fills because the designation signals 'serious swimmers only,' not because fastest swimmers self-selected; job is social belonging in a peer-defined lane; Kiran misread his own fix

examples.scenario: This afternoon, Kiran watches the lane distribution from the spectator bench after new speed designations go up. The fast lane is full. Medium-speed swimmers still crowd the middle, even when the fast lane opens. Exit conversations reveal why: the fast lane sign reads serious swimmers only to anyone who is fast but does not claim that identity. The designation created a peer-defined in-group. Kiran fixed a flow problem and built a belonging barrier in the same move. Kiran must decide whether to remove the social signal or add a parallel lane for fast-but-not-serious swimmers.
examples.whatToDo: Reframe the lane criteria around pace over identity. Use observable benchmarks like yards per minute instead of labels like fast or serious, and watch whether the distribution changes.
examples.whyItMatters: The fix addressed speed management and hired a social sorting function nobody asked for. Kiran learned the job by reading the consequence, not the intention, and now has specific evidence for what to change.

questions.prompt: Emily runs the three-part diagnostic on airport valet parking and discovers the substitute is a phone photo of the parking level, not a competing valet service. What does this finding demonstrate about applying the jobs lens to a new domain?
choices: Price must be the true variable because travelers always respond to cost differences in transportation.
The diagnostic produced a result observable in behavior that contradicts the category-based frame, proving portability through evidence, not assumption.
The substitute set is defined by category membership, so the lens must be wrong if no other valet service appears.
questions.explanation: A phone photo of a parking level beats valet because certainty at midnight is the job, not price or quality. That finding only appears by following local evidence instead of assuming category boundaries define the substitute.

questions.prompt: André finds that plots hired for social belonging go fallow when the neighboring plot-holder moves. A garden coordinator wants to fix this with a stronger renewal email campaign. What is the gap in that response?
choices: The renewal campaign is failing because of messaging quality and timing: if emails arrived earlier in the renewal cycle and used more personalized content about each plot's specific history, they would create enough emotional pull to override the reduced motivation, and the coordinator should A/B test subject lines and send timing before concluding the channel is ineffective.

The problem is plot design and community programming: if the garden had shared tool stations, communal harvest events, and a buddy-plot assignment system, the social connection would not depend on one specific neighbor, and the coordinator should invest in programming that diversifies the belonging job rather than relying on organic neighbor bonds.
Renewal campaigns address commitment signals but cannot reconstruct a circumstance that no longer exists; job evaporation requires re-hiring conditions, not re-engagement messaging.
questions.explanation: When the circumstance that made a hire active disappears, no messaging campaign recreates it. The job ended with the neighbor's move. The response needs to address the circumstance gap, not the communication gap.

questions.prompt: Chiara finds that retained freelance accounting software users engage the CLIENT NOTES field most. Her product team wants to add more invoice templates based on this same churn analysis. What is wrong with that conclusion?
choices: The churn analysis points to relationship-anxiety management as the retention driver; a billing-feature roadmap improves the part of the product that is not driving the hiring decision.

The invoice-template conclusion is correct but the team is drawing it for the wrong reason: retained users engage CLIENT NOTES because noting client mood helps them invoice more accurately, so the real retention driver is richer invoicing context, not anxiety management, and adding smarter invoice templates that pull from call notes would improve retention.

The CLIENT NOTES finding is valid and the product implication is a dedicated client relationship dashboard: since users are managing relationship anxiety, the right move is a structured CRM layer with mood-tracking, follow-up reminders, and relationship health scores, giving the anxiety-management job a first-class product surface rather than leaving it in an unstructured notes field.
questions.explanation: Feature engagement data is evidence of what job is being hired. When retention correlates with CLIENT NOTES over invoice templates, improving billing features responds to assumed demand, not observed hiring behavior.

questions.prompt: James is evaluating a 340-upvote feature request for pronunciation-scoring AI. He finds that sessions where a partner said 'you are easy to understand' cancel thirty percent less often than high-accuracy-score sessions. What should James do before committing the build?
choices: The 340-upvote request is sufficient demand evidence to justify building the AI: upvote counts on feature requests represent revealed preference from engaged users who have already thought about the product, and the cancellation correlation should be validated after the feature ships because pre-launch data cannot substitute for actual usage in a real product context.
Test whether explicit human reassurance reduces cancellations more than any accuracy metric, using the cancellation data as the success measure, not accuracy improvement.

Before committing to any build, James should run a qualitative user research study focused on which features would make users recommend the app to a friend: the cancellation pattern suggests something about the social experience but the team needs richer preference data across the feature set before narrowing to either pronunciation AI or the partner communication hypothesis.
questions.explanation: Upvotes capture the stated want. The cancellation data surfaces the hired job: reducing the emotional cost of trying. Testing reassurance against cancellation rate is the disciplined next step before committing a full AI build.

questions.prompt: Ingrid's color consultation service generates consultees who return to buy mid-range paint instead of premium. An exit interview reveals: 'I just needed someone to say I was not going to ruin it.' Which element of the three-part diagnostic does this quote most directly reveal?
choices: The circumstance that triggered the hire, because it explains when the shopper decided to visit the store.
The substitute set, because it shows what other stores the buyer visited.
The progress being sought: permission to proceed and relief from the anxiety of visible failure in front of neighbors.
questions.explanation: The exit line names the desired end state directly: not expert guidance but the confidence that the decision is defensible. That is the progress dimension of the diagnostic, and it reframes what the consultation service is actually selling.

questions.prompt: Kiran adds speed designations to pool lap lanes and finds that medium-speed swimmers avoid the fast lane even when it is empty, while the fast lane fills with self-identified serious swimmers. He expected a flow outcome. What job did the designation actually serve?
choices: A social belonging job: the designation created a peer-defined in-group that attracted serious-identity swimmers and excluded others regardless of actual pace.

A flow-management job: the label functioned as a self-sorting signal that concentrated the fastest swimmers in one lane, reducing pace-mismatch collisions and increasing throughput, and the medium-speed avoidance reflects rational lane self-selection: if the fast lane is underused by medium swimmers, that confirms the sorting mechanism is working as designed, even if Kiran measured the wrong outcome.

A safety-signaling job: medium-speed swimmers avoided the fast lane because they perceived higher collision risk from faster swimmers in close proximity, not because of identity: the avoidance behavior is self-protective rather than social, and if the pool added a physical buffer marker between the fast and medium lanes, the avoidance pattern would persist because the underlying safety concern would be unchanged.
questions.explanation: The fast lane filled through identity signaling, not pace sorting. The designation hired a social function Kiran did not intend. The distribution only makes sense when read through the belonging job, not the flow problem he was solving.

questions.prompt: A product team hears about the community garden job-evaporation finding and wants to apply it to their subscription app. They write: 'Users who lose their accountability partner will churn.' What is the difference between this claim and a proved job finding?
choices: Subscription cancellation data is more precise than behavioral garden observation because it captures a clear binary event with exact timestamps, enabling statistical analysis that garden behavioral data does not support: so the app team's hypothesis is actually stronger evidence than the garden finding and should be treated as confirmed for planning purposes.

The garden finding was proved by following observable behavior in that specific domain. The app claim is a hypothesis borrowed from analogy; it needs field evidence from that setting to count as proved.

The claims are equivalent because they share the same underlying causal mechanism: social connection loss drives disengagement: and when a mechanism is identified through rigorous observation in one domain, it applies to structurally similar contexts without requiring domain-specific re-proof, since the mechanism is what travels, not just the pattern.
questions.explanation: Analogy produces hypotheses, not proved jobs. André's finding holds because he followed observable evidence in that specific domain. The app team needs local behavioral data before treating the imported conclusion as actionable.

questions.prompt: A service team is applying the three-part diagnostic to a new domain for the first time. They identify the circumstance and progress dimensions clearly but struggle to name the substitute set. What is the most common reason the substitute set stays hidden?
choices: The substitute set should be left undefined until quantitative surveys confirm the options buyers considered.
Substitutes only exist in consumer markets, so the diagnostic does not apply in B2B settings.
Teams look for substitutes within the product category instead of watching what the buyer actually used before, during, or instead of the hire.
questions.explanation: Category thinking keeps the substitute set narrow. The real substitute often lives outside the category, the way a self-park photo substitutes for valet or a neighbor conversation substitutes for a color expert. Observation of actual behavior before the hire surfaces those options.

questions.prompt: After running the three-part diagnostic in five new domains, a researcher concludes that portability is confirmed because the same three questions always produce an answer. A senior colleague pushes back. What is the strongest version of the colleague's objection?
choices: Producing an answer is not the same as producing a proved answer. Portability requires that conclusions hold against observable evidence in each domain, not just that the question format can be applied.

Five domains represents a small sample and the pattern of getting answers each time could reflect that the domains were selected because they are structurally similar to where the method originated, so the researcher should extend to at least fifteen domains spanning commercial, civic, and cultural contexts before claiming portability.

The researcher should publish the five-domain findings and let peer review surface any weaknesses: academic replication by independent researchers provides a more rigorous test of portability than any in-study design could achieve, because peer reviewers will apply the diagnostic in domains the original researcher did not choose.
questions.explanation: A diagnostic that always produces an answer can still produce unproved ones. The colleague's objection is that each conclusion must be earned through local evidence. The question form travels; the conclusions must be re-earned every time.

reviewCards.front: You apply the three-part diagnostic in a new domain and get an unexpected answer. What makes that answer a proved finding and not a guess?
reviewCards.back: The answer is proved when it holds against observable evidence gathered in that specific setting: behavior you can watch, substitutes the buyer actually used, and a progress description the buyer recognizes. An unexpected answer backed by local evidence is stronger than a predicted answer backed by confidence from another domain.

reviewCards.front: A user stops engaging with a product after a change in their personal circumstances. What job-theory term describes this pattern?
reviewCards.back: Job evaporation. The circumstance that made the hire active has ended. The user has not failed to commit; the condition that triggered the job no longer exists. Retention efforts that ignore this distinction will treat a structural gap as a messaging problem.

reviewCards.front: A product team finds the CLIENT NOTES field is the strongest retention predictor in their accounting software. How should they use this finding?
reviewCards.back: Treat it as evidence of the real job being hired. The product is being used to manage relationship anxiety, not billing efficiency. Roadmap priorities, onboarding design, and positioning should all be tested against this job before adding more billing features.

reviewCards.front: You identify the circumstance and the progress for a new job. What is the third piece of the diagnostic, and why does it matter for design?
reviewCards.back: The substitute set: what the buyer used, considered, or fell back on before or instead of your product. The substitute defines the real competitive frame and reveals what good enough already looks like from the buyer's point of view. Without it, improvements may target the wrong variable.

reviewCards.front: A fix intended to solve a flow problem creates an unintended belonging barrier. What discipline would have surfaced this risk before implementation?
reviewCards.back: Asking which jobs the change would serve beyond the stated purpose. Changes to shared spaces and shared systems often trigger social jobs nobody planned for. Running the three-part diagnostic on the new arrangement before launch surfaces unintended hiring functions while they are still easy to redesign.

implementationPlan.title: Applying the Job Diagnostic in New Domains
implementationPlan.coreSkill: Apply the three-part diagnostic in a domain you have not mapped before. Name the circumstance that makes the hire active, describe the progress being sought, and identify what the buyer actually compared or used instead. Let observable evidence in that specific domain confirm or revise your prediction before you act on it.

ifThenPlans.plan: If your team is about to apply a finding from another industry to your product, then run the three-part diagnostic in your own domain first and require local evidence before treating the imported conclusion as actionable.

If a health habit you hired for a specific reason stops feeling useful, then name what circumstance originally triggered the hire and whether that circumstance still exists, before replacing the habit with a new one.
If a subscription, membership, or recurring purchase starts to feel hollow, then write the original hiring circumstance and check whether it is still active or has quietly evaporated.

If a shared activity you and someone else both valued starts going unused, then ask whether the circumstance that made it worth hiring together has changed before assuming motivation or commitment is the issue.

implementationPlan.twentyFourHourChallenge: Pick one product or service you use regularly in a category unrelated to your work. Write out the three-part diagnostic: the circumstance that makes you hire it, the progress you are seeking, and what you have compared or substituted in the past. If the diagnostic reveals a job different from the product's stated purpose, you have just run a portable field test.
implementationPlan.weeklyPractice: Once this week, pick a domain you know nothing about and interview one person who regularly uses a product or service in that domain. Apply the three-part diagnostic strictly: circumstance, progress, substitutes. Record where your prediction was wrong before the evidence came in.

memorableLines.text: You do not carry the answer. You carry the discipline of asking: what situation made this person reach for something, what would a better version of this situation feel like, and what else was this person comparing in that moment.
memorableLines.why: It captures the central paradox of portability and names the three questions in one retrievable passage.
